goals.0: Connect to the service on port 5842, sum the four uint32 values it sends, return the sum to receive the vortex1 credentials.
goals.1: Get a shell from /vortex/vortex1: walk its cursor 261 backslashes to the saved frame pointer and send four raw 0xca bytes (the getchar hook only filters keyboard input, not a pipe) so the cursor's top byte becomes 0xca.
goals.2: Get the vortex3 password. /vortex/vortex2 (setuid vortex3) runs `tar cf /tmp/ownership.$$.tar <our args>`; with /etc/vortex_pass/vortex3 as the only argument tar archives the password file into a vortex3-owned archive we can copy and extract.
goals.3: Get the vortex4 password. /vortex/vortex3 (setuid root) copies argv[1] into a 128-byte buffer and then writes the buffer address into the GOT slot named by lpp; put 69 bytes of NUL-free shellcode in the buffer and set lpp to exit's GOT slot (0x804b200), so the next call to exit jumps onto the executable stack.
goals.4: Get the vortex5 password. /vortex/vortex4 (setuid vortex5) calls printf(argv[3]), but with argc==1 and an empty argv[0] it reaches printf on envp[1]: the format string is the second environment variable. Two %hn writes through vararg slots 125 and 126 overwrite exit's GOT slot with the shellcode address, and exit jumps into 69 bytes of shellcode on the executable stack.
goals.5: Get the vortex6 password. /vortex/vortex5 (setuid vortex6) checks the MD5 of the entered password against a fixed digest; brute-force the 5-character alphanumeric preimage with a multiprocess search and use the password to get a shell as vortex6.
goals.6: Get the vortex7 password. /vortex/vortex6 (setuid vortex7) re-execs argv[0] as root; run it with argv[0] set to /bin/sh, so restart re-execs a shell with real uid vortex7.
goals.7: Get the vortex8 password. /vortex/vortex7 (setuid vortex8) only runs strcpy on argv[1] when its CRC32 is 0xe1ca95ee; solve the CRC patch with a GF(2) linear system, then overflow the 350-byte buffer with a NOP sled and setreuid shellcode on the executable stack, delivered by a raw-bytes argv driver.
goals.8: Get the vortex9 password. /vortex/vortex8 (setuid vortex9) drops its euid before overflowing, but the safecode thread it spawned keeps euid vortex9; overwrite sleep's GOT slot to hijack the thread, sweep the buffer address with a uid-signature shellcode, then run a password shellcode that reads /etc/vortex_pass/vortex9 — over ssh -T, since a pty drags the thread's euid down.
goals.9: Get the vortex10 password. There is no /vortex/vortex9 binary and /vortex/vortex10 is unreachable from vortex9, but /var/mail/vortex9 holds the vortex10 password in plain text; read it and log in as vortex10.
goals.10: Get the vortex11 password. /vortex/vortex10 (setuid vortex11) seeds rand() with a time-derived value and prints 20 rand() outputs; brute-force the seed with the target's own libc rand, then send the seed as 4 raw little-endian bytes to get a shell as vortex11.
goals.11: Get the vortex12 password. /vortex/vortex11 (setuid vortex12) embeds its own phkmalloc; overflow the strcpy on argv[1] to corrupt the next page's header, aim the next malloc at exit@GOT with a fake chunk, overwrite it with a shellcode address via the 15-byte strncpy on argv[2], and land in a NOP-sled EGG variable that reads /etc/vortex_pass/vortex12 -- pin the EGG address with a -m32 helper run with the same argv.
